title: Tower Maze Defense (v25)
description: Tower defense with procedurally generated looping/splitting mazes, now with smooth outlined path rendering, directional arrows, and clear corner visuals.
prompt:
In our TD game, The path is rendered as a series of grey tiles on a grid. I have a visual clarity problem I need you to fix.

The problem:

The path is hard to read visually. Specifically:

Direction is ambiguous. Looking at the path, a player cannot tell which direction enemies travel or which way the route flows. It just looks like a collection of grey squares.

Parallel segments merge visually. In sections where the path folds back on itself (U-turns, S-bends, or where one segment runs alongside another), the adjacent tiles blend together into a single grey blob. There's no visual gap or separation, so you can't tell where one leg of the path ends and the next begins, or which tile connects to which.

Turns and corners look like stacked squares rather than a continuous flowing line.


What I need you to implement:

Path outlining. Give the path a distinct border/outline (a slightly lighter or darker edge) so that when two segments run parallel, there's a clear visible boundary between them instead of a merged blob.

Proper corner rendering. Render turns as smooth/rounded connectors that visually flow around bends, rather than as hard stacked squares, so the path reads as one continuous line.
